advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Constrain `_MAKE_WORKFLOW_CALL`'s args capture to a single line (e.g. use `[^;&|\n]+` or apply the regex per-line) so make-target discovery cannot span newlines and seed phantom targets.
evidence: tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py:1683-1688: `for match in _MAKE_WORKFLOW_CALL.finditer(_live_make_lines(text)): for token in match.group("args").split(): ... if _MAKE_TARGET.fullmatch(token): targets.add(token)`
`_live_make_lines` joins lines with `\n` (line 1677), and a Python negated character class matches `\n`, so the args capture is not line-bounded.

Phantom targets pollute `_reachable_make_targets` (which does not filter against `_make_recipe_bodies`), so both positive subset assertions and negative `"worktree" not in reachable` / `"worktree" not in recipes` assertions could be silently corrupted if a future run body introduces separator-less multi-line make usage.
advisory.finding: `_MAKE_WORKFLOW_CALL`'s args group `(?P<args>(?:\s+[^;&|]+)+)` uses a negated class `[^;&|]` that also matches newlines, so when a multi-line workflow `run:` body has a `make <target>` line followed by another command line NOT separated by `;`, `&`, or `|`, the match greedily spans the newline and captures words from subsequent lines. Those words are then split and any that fullmatch `_MAKE_TARGET` become phantom seeded targets (e.g. `make lint`\n`echo done` yields phantom targets `echo` and `done`).
scenarios: A future workflow `run:` block places `make lint` on its own line followed by an unrelated command line without a `;`/`&&`/`|` separator.
The captured phantom token happens to equal a real Make target that CI does not actually invoke, breaking a negative assertion.
advisory.suggested_fix: Change the args character class to exclude newlines: `(?P<args>(?:\s+[^;&|\n]+)+)`, or run `_targets_from_make_invocations` line-by-line instead of over newline-joined text.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add per-construct positive-detection assertions (a table over `_MAKE_NON_POSIX_CONSTRUCTS`) so each of the double-bracket, array, here-string, and case-modification detectors is proven to fire on a known bash-only input.
evidence: tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py:1652-1664 defines detectors for 'set -o pipefail', 'double-bracket test' (`\[\[`), 'indexed/associative array', 'here-string' (`<<<`), and 'case-modification'
search for 'double-bracket' and 'here-string' returns ONLY the definition line (1654, 1662) — no test references them

The only positive detection asserted is `set -o pipefail`: test_static_recipe_scan_reaches_transitive_make_targets (line 1856-1858) and the seeded control in test_ci_reachable_make_recipes_reject_bash_only_constructs (line 1894-1896)

ABSENCE rationale: without a table-driven positive assertion per detector, a broken regex (e.g. an unescaped `[[` or wrong array pattern) passes the whole suite while the scanner it powers no longer catches that construct — the safety property the diff introduces is unenforced for 4/5 of its constructs
advisory.finding: Four of the five newly-added non-POSIX-dash detector regexes in `_MAKE_NON_POSIX_CONSTRUCTS` (double-bracket test, indexed/associative array, here-string, case-modification) are never exercised by a positive-detection test; only `set -o pipefail` is. A regex error in any of the four would silently fail to detect the bash-only construct it targets, and every test would remain green.
scenarios: A future edit corrupts the `[[` or `<<<` or array regex; a bash-only Makefile recipe using that construct now hides behind a green lane, which is precisely the failure this patch claims to prevent
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a parametrized test that feeds a minimal recipe body for each construct (e.g. `\t[[ -z "$x" ]]`, `\techo <<< foo`, `\tdeclare -A m`, `\techo ${x^^}`) through `_bash_only_make_recipe_violations` and asserts the corresponding label is reported.
